chapter: Queens Terrace, Decca records and Amen
title: Billy Shaw, the Ritz Carlton, the Plain in Duluth and the Beachcomber
summary: With Billy Shaw's agency he plays top clubs from Boston to Duluth and Omaha.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Yeah, I got nice money. Then after "Amen" I got fantastic money, to what I'd been making. You see, after we went into--after we came out of McGuinney's, I went--Billy Shaw took me over there, Billy Shaw was with the William Morris Agency, he picked me up and that's when I got into the real big money.
Oh yeah?
I jumped into the Ritz Carlton Hotel in Boston.
Oh, that is big money, sure.
That was the biggest you could get. From then--
What is it, '43 now?
Oh, still '42.
Fall or winter of '42.
Fall of '42.
So then we left there, they booked me into the Stagecoach Inn, it was big then, in Jersey.
Fort Lee or someplace like that.
I don't think it's Fort Lee; it's on the highway.
I think I heard of it before.
It was a very famous place.
From then they jumped me out to the Duluth, Minnesota, a place called the Plain.
In Duluth?
Duluth. They got one in Minneapolis too, but it was nothing compared with the Plain. That was one of the finest clubs-- I was broadcasting at NBC.
Who was working with you now, it wasn't Buster Smith?
I got Willard Brown back. I got the same guys that started with me, Frank Clark on bass, Bob Carroll, Willard Brown, Godley and Call Cobbs.
Call Cobbs you picked up here in New York?
Right. We went to the Plain and as I said, one of the finest jobs I ever had. That was the first of three times that I went in the Plain.
From the Plain we went into the Beachcomber in Omaha. I followed Nat King Cole in there. All these were high clubs.
Good money.
Good money jobs.
